2O.1 We are required to give thanks to God.

precepts.text: The sun to rule by day, the moon and stars by night, him that smote Egypt in their firstborn, brought out Israel with a strong hand, divided the Red Sea, overthrew Pharaoh, led his people through the wilderness, and smote great kings: for his mercy endureth forever. He killed our enemies because he had mercy on us, and we saw all of it and still do evil. There is no temptation that should derail us from the wide place, because his mercies endure forever.
precepts.point: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man; God will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able, but will with the temptation make a way to escape. If you understand the joy of the elect you embrace the temptation, because he has your back. He wants you to make it, though there are those appointed to die. Nobody wanted to pay a landlord who tripled the rent in Brooklyn after counting heads across the street; that trial forced us to pool the real estate, carpentry, plumbing, and electrical talent the Lord had among us, and then he blessed us with the building in New York despite the detractors. We never took our eyes off the prize. Do not let anyone take your crown.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
Paul says God “will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape”. There is no temptation that should derail us from inheriting the wide place, the kingdom that sits within the narrow passage (2 Esdras 7), because God's mercies endure for ever. David shows that mercy: “The sun to rule by day: for his mercy endureth for ever: The moon and stars to rule by night: for his mercy endureth for ever.” The Lord declared the end from the beginning and created all of this. We acknowledge his greatness and his mercy, and we tap into that comfort under the shadow of his wings.

“To him that smote Egypt in their firstborn: for his mercy endureth for ever: And brought out Israel from among them”. The Most High killed our enemies for us because he had mercy on us. We cried in Egypt, the Lord heard our cries and said, go down, Moses, tell Pharaoh to let my people go, or I will kill his firstborn.

“With a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm”, “To him which divided the Red sea into parts”, “And made Israel to pass through the midst of it”, “But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red sea”, “To him which led his people through the wilderness”, “To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever”.

We saw all of this, and we still get here today and do evil, just as our fathers under the cloud did. The Most High is trying to set us back up, but he wants to make sure we are in the right spiritual posture to inherit the kingdom. He lets us use his Bible as spiritual weapons to fight off the evil temptations so we can get to the wide.
